subject: Temporary deviation request: on-call coverage contingency during DC migration
messages:
From: Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Sam Lee <sam@acmecloud.com>, Jonas Petersen <jonas@dcops.net>
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 08:14:00 -0800
Subject: Temporary deviation request: on-call coverage contingency during DC migration

Hi Laura / Stephanie —

Quick note to request a short, defined deviation from our standard P1/P2 on-call rota for the weekend of Nov 21–22. AcmeCloud (their netops team copied) will be performing a critical migration of our secondary inference cluster (EU region) that may temporarily reduce our ability to route cross-region failover without a manual intervention window. They estimate a 6–8 hour maintenance window with potential for transient increased latency (~200–400ms) and a small chance of degraded KV cache availability for managed sessions.

What I’m asking for:
- Approval for a temporary on-call swap so we can consolidate senior support into a single response path for that 8-hour window (reduce rotation to one P1 primary + one P2 backup instead of the usual staggered night overlap).
- Authorization to use the fallback escalation path in the contingency matrix (attached) that routes immediate P1 ownership to the Dedicated infra on-call and points any customer-facing triage to the CS on-call.
- Agreement on a timeboxed SLA deviation: during the window we set P1 response target to 30 minutes (rather than 15) with explicit commitments to notify any impacted customers and to issue a post-mortem within 72 hours.

Mitigations included:
- Pre-migration canarying and throttled traffic to reduce KV-sensitivity.
- Prefix cache warming script (Jonas is coordinating) prior to the window.
- Pager tags and alert thresholds adjusted to suppress non-actionable noise.

Attachments: contingency_matrix_v2.xlsx (detailed fallback routing + contact tree), oncall_swap_schedule.ics

If you’re ok with the approach I’ll:
1) Notify impacted accounts (AcmeCloud + top 10 latency-sensitive customers) with proposed timeline and opt-out window.
2) Lock the on-call swaps in PagerDuty and add the temporary escalation rule.
3) Run the cache warm script with Jonas on Nov 20.

Goal is to keep customer-facing impact minimal while allowing the DC migration to proceed. Need a sign-off by end-of-day Nov 12 to complete operational prep.

Thanks —
Rohan Mehta
Head of Support Operations
Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 (415) 555-0147

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Sam Lee <sam@acmecloud.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 10:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Temporary deviation request: on-call coverage contingency during DC migration

Rohan —

Thanks for the summary. A couple quick questions before I can greenlight the kernel-level routing changes from the infra side: 

1) Do we have estimated token-rate/throughput numbers for the canary groups you plan to run? I need to validate the kernel memory pressure assumptions against the Dedicated pool before we consolidate on-call.
2) For the 30-minute P1 target: will you include a mandatory escalation to a named infra owner at 30 minutes (i.e., auto-escalate to Marcus Lin or on-call equivalent)? Right now our PD rule auto-escalates at 15/30/60 — I want to avoid silent periods.
3) Please confirm whether the deviation applies only to US time zones or also to APAC/EU customers. Sam — please confirm AcmeCloud’s dependencies (we’d prefer not to impact their EU read replica).

If you can send the throughput numbers and the updated PD escalation snippet I’ll run a quick safety validation and try to sign off today.

Best,
Laura
Director, Platform Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Jonas Petersen <jonas@dcops.net>, Sam Lee <sam@acmecloud.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 12:38:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Temporary deviation request: on-call coverage contingency during DC migration

Laura — thanks, answers below and I’ve attached the contingency matrix with explicit PD snippets and escalation names.

1) Canary throughput: planned canary group is ~7% of normal production token rate (about 18k tokens/sec aggregate for the canary traffic) with 5% variance. We’ll throttle if latency exceeds 250ms sustained for >5 minutes. Full numbers are in the attached sheet (contingency_matrix_v2.xlsx) under the "Canary traffic" tab.

2) Escalation: yes — PD will have an automatic escalation to Marcus Lin after 30 minutes; Marcus is listed as infra lead for the weekend. PD rules we’ll apply for the window: notify P1 primary immediately, escalate to Marcus at 30 minutes, escalate to Stephanie at 60 minutes. The PD JSON snippet is included in the attachment and I can paste it into infra if needed.

3) Scope: this deviation is US-only (we’re migrating the secondary US cluster). No EU/APAC customers should be affected, and we’ll keep EU routing unchanged. Sam, Jonas: can you confirm respective replica boundaries and that their read-only EU replica isn’t touched?

Next steps I’ll take if I get approvals:
- Lock the on-call swap in PD and publish the temporary routing rule (Nov 13).
- Provide the PD rule JSON to Marcus and ops for review.
- Draft customer notifications and run by Legal for wording.

I’ve also added Mina to loop for compliance sign-off on the post-mortem SLA note.

Attachments: contingency_matrix_v2.xlsx

—
Rohan Mehta
Head of Support Operations

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Sam Lee <sam@acmecloud.com>, Jonas Petersen <jonas@dcops.net>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 14:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Temporary deviation request: on-call coverage contingency during DC migration

Thanks everyone — I’ve reviewed the contingency matrix and the PD escalation snippet. I approve the temporary, timeboxed deviation with the following conditions: 

1) Timebox: deviation allowed only for Nov 21 02:00–10:00 UTC (US night window). Any extension requires written approval from myself + Marcus Lin.
2) Customer comms: send an initial notification to impacted customers by Nov 13 COB and provide an opt-out for customers who cannot accept the 30-minute P1 SLA during the window. Legal review must be attached to the notification.
3) Post-mortem: a joint CS + Infra post-mortem is required within 72 hours and must include token-level latency histograms and a summary of any mitigation actions.
4) Compliance: Mina, please confirm that the wording on the notification and the post-mortem retention meet our data handling and audit requirements — if any additional retention notes are needed we will include them.

I’ll mark this approved in the change tracker (SUP-2123) and expect Rohan to implement the PD rules and customer comms per timeline. Please keep me posted on any blocker.

Approved —
Stephanie Nguyen
VP, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
